feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Australia had its second-warmest September on record and its warmest September nights
entry.summary: Australia's September 2026 ran 2.71 °C above average, and minimum temperatures were the highest on record for the month. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology September 2026 summary, via Weatherzone, 1 October 2026

entry.title: France had its second-warmest September since 1900 and a record soil drought
entry.summary: France's September 2026 ran 3.1 °C above normal, the fourth month in a row above 3 °C. — Sources: Météo-France, September 2026 climate summary, 2 October 2026

entry.title: Southern California is under a seven-day October heat warning as grid demand forecasts rise
entry.summary: A heat warning covers Los Angeles, San Diego and inland Orange County from 2 to 8 October, with valley highs to 107 °F. — Sources: National Weather Service · California Independent System Operator, via Bloomberg, 2 October 2026 · San Diego Gas & Electric, via KPBS, 2 October 2026 · Cal/OSHA advisory 2026-79, 2 October 2026

entry.title: Storms fed by a sea 4 °C warmer than normal shut schools for 400,000 pupils in eastern Spain
entry.summary: With sea temperatures off eastern Spain about 4 °C above normal, more than 200 litres per square metre of rain fell on 1 and 2 October, 90 in one hour at Castellón. — Sources: Euronews, 2 October 2026 · AEMET

entry.title: Paraguay and Argentina set heat records in South America's first spring heatwave
entry.summary: Paraguay's Mariscal Estigarribia reached 43.8 °C on 28 September, beating a record from 1952, and 14 Paraguayan localities set records that day. — Sources: Paraguay Directorate of Meteorology and Hydrology, via El Litoral · INMET Brazil, via Agência Brasil, 28 September 2026

entry.title: The United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Belgium each had a top-five warm September
entry.summary: The United Kingdom had its joint-fourth warmest September since 1884, peaking at 28.1 °C on 29 September. — Sources: Met Office, 1 October 2026 · KNMI, 30 September 2026 · Royal Meteorological Institute of Belgium, via VRT, 1 October 2026

entry.title: Correction: the Netherlands' 30 September record was 27.1 °C at Hupsel
entry.summary: The highest 30 September reading ever measured in the Netherlands was 27.1 °C at Hupsel, beating 26.7 °C set at Winterswijk in 1895. — Sources: Weeronline, citing KNMI, 30 September 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's fires keep haze risk high over Malaysia and Singapore into November
entry.summary: Regional haze risk over Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore stays high through November, and Indonesia's weather agency expects meaningful monsoon rain only in late October or early November. — Sources: ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre · Indonesia Agency for Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics, via Tempo

entry.title: Spain attributed 556 deaths to heat in September 2026
entry.summary: Spain's daily mortality monitoring system attributed 556 deaths to heat in September and 2,149 in August. September was provisionally Spain's warmest since 1961, at 3.3 °C above normal. — Sources: Carlos III Health Institute MoMo system, via eldiario.es, 1 October 2026 · AEMET provisional estimate, 24 September 2026

entry.title: France counted 7,824 excess deaths across its three summer heatwaves
entry.summary: France's public health agency counted 5,764 excess deaths in the 17 June to 2 July heatwave, 1,243 from 3 to 22 July and 817 from 27 July to 20 August. The figures are provisional. — Sources: Santé publique France, provisional, September 2026

entry.title: Kenya and South Sudan pilot the Horn of Africa's first heat-health early warning system
entry.summary: The regional climate centre ICPAC is piloting heat-health warnings in Nairobi, Kenya and Juba, South Sudan until August 2027. — Sources: ICPAC, 4 September 2026

entry.title: A 24-year-old farmworker died of heat exposure harvesting sweet potatoes in Mississippi
entry.summary: Obed Azahel Hernandez Perez died on 8 September at a farm in Vardaman, Mississippi, with a heat index near 98 °F. — Sources: Mississippi Today, 1 October 2026

entry.title: South Korea found four break-rule violations in 1,197 worksites in its heat-break rule's second year
entry.summary: South Korea requires a 20-minute break every two hours at an apparent temperature of 33 °C. — Sources: Ministry of Employment and Labor and KOSHA, via Seoul Economic Daily, 28 September 2026
